To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elastomers used in robotics are time- and history-dependent, and that strain gauge output can be used to measure deformation without the need for recalibration.
elastomers used in the design of soft robots exhibit a variety of nonlinear behaviors and that these effects can be decoupled from the strain measurement of embedded resistive strain gages.

the mechanical properties of elastomers used in robotic applications are time-dependent and nonlinear, and that embedded resistive strain sensors are a robust method for characterizing the deformation of elastomeric materials.

the effects of nonlinear and time-dependent material properties in soft materials used in soft robotic applications.
the effects of the material properties of elastomers on the performance of soft robotic systems.
the characterization of soft materials and their effects on the performance of embedded sensing devices.

the material characterization of these elastomers is not trivial and that the effects of the time-dependent, nonlinear material response should be accounted for in dynamic modeling and control of soft robotic systems.

these materials show a high degree of repeatability and robustness to loading conditions and that the measured strain from the resistive strain gauge is a reliable measure of the material strain, regardless of the material properties.
